title: trailboss --json agents ls
description: Every agent definition `task add --agent <name>` can start, repo ones first, then yours, then the built-in one per agent kind; names sorted within each. Broken definitions are listed with their problem.

name.description: What `task add --agent` takes: the file's name without `.json`, or the agent kind for a built-in one.

kind.description: claude, codex, gemini, copilot, opencode or pi; more may be added. Empty when the file couldn't be read.

source.description: repo (the repository's `.trailboss/agents/`), user (`~/.config/trailboss/agents/`) or built-in. A name from an earlier source wins.

path.description: The definition's file; null when built in.

active.description: Whether this is the one its name starts: false when a definition earlier in repo, user, built-in order has the same name.

args.description: Flags and their values, from the allowlist `resume` keeps, after the model and before the brief.

rules.description: Text put before the brief, a blank line between.

problem.description: Why it can't be started (unreadable, an unknown key or kind, a flag off the allowlist or missing its value, one that would take the brief as its value); null when it can.

trust.description: A repository definition's trust: trusted (`agents trust --yes` recorded this file with this content), new (never trusted) or changed (its content differs from what was trusted). `task add` starts a repository's definition only when trusted. Null for yours and built-in ones, which need no trust.

shadows.description: The sources (user, built-in) of definitions with the same name that this one wins over, in order; empty when it replaces none or isn't active. A repository definition named claude, codex, … replaces the built-in one.
